Which interval should I use?

Source: vignettes/articles/guide-intervals.qmd

medfit gives several intervals. This page says which to reach for, shows them side by side on one dataset, and states what each one assumes. It makes no coverage claim beyond what the package’s tests show.

Pick by situation

Your situation Use Why
A quick look, one mediator, a decent sample tidy(fit, conf_int = TRUE) or confint() delta method: instant, and assumes the estimate is roughly normal
The indirect effect a * b, a final result parametric bootstrap: med(boot = TRUE) draws from the estimated normal distribution of the paths, so the skew of a product shows up
You doubt that normality nonparametric bootstrap resamples rows and refits, so it does not rely on a normal approximation
Serial mediators fitted from lm objects nonparametric bootstrap, or a lavaan fit the lm route sets the covariances among chain paths to zero; see Serial mediation
Weights se_type = "sandwich" robust (heteroskedasticity-consistent) standard errors; see Weights and robust SEs
Treatment assigned to clusters, 25 or more model-based intervals for the paths the engine warns below 25 clusters
Treatment assigned to clusters, fewer than 25 se_type = "kr" for the paths; bootstrap_mediation(cluster = ) for the products see Cluster-randomized trials
A test that the indirect effect is zero mbco_sem() (native engine) minimum of two likelihood-ratio tests; see constraints and MBCO
Only a point estimate the plugin method it has no interval; the bounds are NA

The same fit, four ways

One simple mediation on mediation_demo:

library(medfit)

Attaching package: 'medfit'
The following object is masked from 'package:stats':

    decompose
library(generics)

Attaching package: 'generics'
The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    as.difftime, as.factor, as.ordered, intersect, is.element, setdiff,
    setequal, union
fy <- outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2
fm <- mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
fit <- fit_mediation(fy, fm, data = mediation_demo,
                     treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1")

Delta method (the default in tidy()):

tidy(fit, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)[1, ]
# A tibble: 1 × 5
  term  estimate std_error conf_low conf_high
  <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie      0.333    0.0645    0.206     0.459

Parametric bootstrap (what med(boot = TRUE) runs). The statistic is the product of the two paths, named as bootstrap_mediation() sees them:

indirect <- function(theta) theta["m_treatment"] * theta["y_mediator1"]
par_boot <- bootstrap_mediation(indirect, method = "parametric",
                                mediation_data = fit, n_boot = 2000, seed = 1)
c(lower = par_boot@ci_lower, upper = par_boot@ci_upper)
    lower     upper
0.2107017 0.4689658

Nonparametric bootstrap (resamples rows and refits):

refit_nie <- function(d) {
  unname(nie(fit_mediation(fy, fm, data = d, treatment = "treatment",
                           mediator = "mediator1")))
}
np_boot <- bootstrap_mediation(refit_nie, method = "nonparametric",
                               data = mediation_demo, n_boot = 1000, seed = 1)
c(lower = np_boot@ci_lower, upper = np_boot@ci_upper)
    lower     upper
0.2100149 0.4682970

Plugin (a point estimate only):

plug <- bootstrap_mediation(indirect, method = "plugin", mediation_data = fit)
c(estimate = unname(plug@estimate), lower = plug@ci_lower, upper = plug@ci_upper)
 estimate     lower     upper
0.3327695        NA        NA

On this dataset the three intervals agree to within about 0.01, which is what to expect when the sample is large and the model is simple. They part ways with small samples, skewed variables, weights or few clusters.

What each one assumes

Interval Assumes Cost
Delta method the estimate is approximately normal, with the standard error from the model none
Parametric bootstrap the path estimates are approximately jointly normal fast; no refitting
Nonparametric bootstrap the rows are independent draws slow; refits every time
Plugin nothing; it gives no interval none
Kenward-Roger a linear mixed model with a random intercept needs pbkrtest
Cluster bootstrap clusters are the independent units refits every time; some refits may fail

All the bootstrap intervals are percentile intervals (the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles for a 95% interval). BCa and studentized intervals are not implemented.

Two messages to expect

confint(fit, parm = "effects") warns that the normal approximation for the indirect effect may be inaccurate. That is a nudge toward the bootstrap, not an error; tidy() gives the same delta-method interval without the warning.

A bootstrap warns when refits fail and are dropped; see Troubleshooting.

Limits

  • No coverage claim. This page shows intervals from one dataset; it does not show that they cover 95% of the time. The evidence for the cluster bootstrap on the 2-1-1 design is thin; Methods and Formulas says so.
  • Percentile intervals only.
  • Standard errors under weights need se_type = "sandwich" (the sandwich treats observations as independent).
